back: SO₂: burning sulfur-containing coal/oil and smelting sulfides. NOₓ: N₂ + O₂ → 2NO in hot combustion.
CaCO₃ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + CO₂; 2CaSO₃ + O₂ → 2CaSO₄ (gypsum, CaSO₄·2H₂O).
2NaOH + SO₂ → Na₂SO₃ + H₂O; Ca(OH)₂ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + H₂O.
Coal burned with limestone: CaO traps SO₂ as CaSO₄; lower temperature (below about 900 °C) gives less NOₓ.
Excess air: more complete combustion, less CO and hydrocarbons; NOₓ harder to reduce in a normal converter.
Pt/Pd/Rh: 2CO + 2NO → 2CO₂ + N₂; 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂; hydrocarbons → CO₂ + H₂O. Poisoned by lead.
Coal: reliable but CO₂, SO₂, NOₓ, ash. Hydro: renewable, no emissions, but flooding and drought-dependent.
No CO₂ in operation and little fuel; but long-lived radioactive waste, accident risk (Chernobyl 1986, Fukushima 2011), cost.
Alpha-emitting gas from uranium decay in rocks; collects in unventilated buildings and mines; raises lung-cancer risk.
